## Moist adiabatic extrapolation and the effective heat capacity (`extrapolate_dlnp`, `extrapolate_dz`) {#sec-ch03-adiabat}

### Summary

A parcel that rises adiabatically cools, and when it is saturated part of the cooling is offset by the latent heat of
the condensate it forms. kintera builds such a profile one step at a time: given an equilibrated state at one
pressure (or height), `ThermoX` finds the temperature at the next pressure that conserves the parcel's molar
entropy, equilibrating the phases at every trial temperature. The Newton step of that search needs the derivative
of entropy with respect to temperature *along the saturation curve*, which is the frozen heat capacity plus a
latent term; that sum is the effective heat capacity, and the latent term is read off the gain matrix that the
saturation solver of @sec-ch04 returns. An option drops the condensate after each step for a
pseudo-adiabat. This is the moist adiabat with several condensing species of Li, Ingersoll and Oyafuso
([J. Atmos. Sci. 75, 1063, 2018](https://doi.org/10.1175/JAS-D-17-0257.1)), written for an arbitrary set of
nucleation reactions, with the entropy of @sec-ch03-entropy as its conserved quantity.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Step $(T, p, x)$ along an adiabat by $\Delta\ln p$ or $\Delta z$, conserving molar entropy;
the effective heat capacity is @eq-ch03-adiabat-cp-eff.

**Data.** In and out, in place: $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], mole fractions $x_i$ of all species; parameters
$\Delta\ln p$ or $\Delta z$ [m] with $g$ [$\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$]; optional entropy source per step.

**Placement.** `ThermoX.extrapolate_dlnp` and `ThermoX.extrapolate_dz`; `ThermoX.effective_cp` on its own after
any `forward`.

**Activation.** Called explicitly by a host or script; `rainout` (default off) drops the condensates after each step;
`ds_dlnp` or `ds_dz` (default 0) adds an entropy source; `max-iter` and `ftol` of the card bound the search.

**Guarantee / limits.** Entropy conserved to $10\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ per step (the stopping test); first-order
accurate in the step size; `dz` steps iterate hydrostatic balance with the mean density of the step.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below: `DeviceTest.extrapolate_ad` (entropy to $10^{-3}$), the deep-Jupiter example
(entropy to $10^{-5}\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$, dry limit to $10^{-5}\,\mathrm K$).
:::

Local symbols: $s$ the molar entropy of the parcel, all species counted [$\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$]
($S/\sum_i c_i$); $\xi_j$ the extent of reaction $j$ per mole of parcel [-]; $\mathsf G$ the gain matrix of the
saturation solver, $G_{jk} = \partial r_j/\partial \xi_k$ with $r_j$ the saturation residual of @sec-ch04
(`gain`); $L'_j = \mathrm dL_j/\mathrm dT$; $c_{p}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ the effective molar heat capacity
[$\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$]; $g$ the gravitational acceleration, positive downward [$\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$];
$\bar M = \sum_i x_i M_i$ the mean molar mass. The internal names are `effective_cp`, `extrapolate_dlnp`,
`extrapolate_dz`; the options object is `ExtrapOptions`.

### Derivation

**The effective heat capacity.** At fixed pressure, along the saturation curve, the parcel's enthalpy changes with
temperature both through the heat capacities and through the extents of the phase changes:
$$
\frac{\mathrm dH}{\mathrm dT}\Bigr|_{p,\,\mathrm{sat}} = \sum_i x_i c_{p,i} + \sum_j \Bigl(\sum_i h_i \nu_{ij}\Bigr)\frac{\mathrm d\xi_j}{\mathrm dT} .
$$
The extents follow the saturation conditions $r_j(T, \boldsymbol\xi) = 0$ of the active
reactions (@sec-ch04). Differentiating along the curve, $\sum_k G_{jk}\,\mathrm d\xi_k/\mathrm dT = \partial r_j/\partial T$,
and since $r_j$ depends on $T$ only through $-L_j(T)$, the right-hand side is $L'_j(T)$ up to the sign convention of
the solver's gain matrix. kintera therefore solves the linear system
$$
\mathsf G\,\frac{\mathrm d\boldsymbol\xi}{\mathrm dT} = \mathbf L', \qquad
c_p^{\mathrm{eff}} = \sum_i x_i\,c_{p,i} + \sum_j \Bigl(\sum_i h_i \nu_{ij}\Bigr)\frac{\mathrm d\xi_j}{\mathrm dT},
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-cp-eff}
where $\mathsf G$ is the gain matrix returned by the last `forward`, zero outside the active reactions.
@eq-ch03-adiabat-cp-eff is computed in `ThermoXImpl::effective_cp`
({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::effective_cp >}}), with $L'_j$ from `LogSVPFunc::grad`
({{< code src/thermo/log_svp.hpp LogSVPFunc::grad >}}) and $h_i$, $c_{p,i}$ from @sec-ch03-caloric. For one vapour
condensing in a carrier gas the gain is the scalar $G = 1/x_{\mathrm g} - 1/x_v$ (`[C1]` of `adiabat_check.py`),
$\sum_i h_i\nu_{ij} = h_c - h_v = -\ell$, and the latent term becomes
$$
c_p^{\mathrm{latent}} = \ell\,L'\,\frac{x_v x_{\mathrm g}}{x_{\mathrm g} - x_v}
\;\xrightarrow{\;x_v \ll x_{\mathrm g}\;}\; x_v\,\frac{\ell^2}{\mathcal R T^2},
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-latent-single}
using $L' = \ell/(\mathcal R T^2)$ for an ideal vapour: the classical moist correction (`[C2]`). For the water case
of @fig-ch03-adiabat-effective-cp at $290\,\mathrm K$ and $1\,\mathrm{bar}$ the latent term is $1.3$ times the frozen
heat capacity (`[C3]`).

The linear solve is ill-conditioned when one active reaction involves a nearly depleted vapour: that reaction's row
of $\mathsf G$ is scaled by $1/x_v$ and can be $10^{12}$ times larger than the row that carries the latent heat, and a
least-squares solver with a relative rank tolerance drops exactly the small row. The code therefore divides each
row of $\mathsf G$ and the matching entry of $\mathbf L'$ by the row's largest magnitude before the solve (the same
solution in exact arithmetic, condition number of order one), solves with the `gelsd` driver on CPU (whose pivoting,
unlike the default driver's, does not depend on uninitialised memory) and with a pseudo-inverse of absolute tolerance
$10^{-6}$ on CUDA; a zero row (inactive reaction) keeps scale one and a zero rate.

**Stepping in pressure.** The parcel's molar entropy $s_0$ at the start is the target. After multiplying the pressure
by $e^{\Delta\ln p}$, each pass restores the starting composition, equilibrates it at the current $T$
(`forward`, which also returns $\mathsf G$), evaluates $s(T)$ and $c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}$, and updates
$$
T \leftarrow T\Bigl(1 + \frac{s_{\mathrm{target}} - s(T)}{c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}}\Bigr), \qquad
s_{\mathrm{target}} = s_0 + \frac{\mathrm ds}{\mathrm d\ln p}\,\Delta\ln p ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-newton}
until $|s_{\mathrm{target}} - s(T)| < 10\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ (in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$, an absolute
test) or `max-iter` passes. @eq-ch03-adiabat-newton is computed in `ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dlnp`
({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dlnp >}}). It is the Newton step on
$s(T) - s_{\mathrm{target}}$ with $\partial s/\partial T|_{p,\mathrm{sat}} = c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}/T$, linearised in $T$
instead of $\ln T$; the remainder of one step is $c_p\,\delta^2/2$ with $\delta = (s_{\mathrm{target}} - s)/c_p$,
so the convergence is quadratic (`[C4]`). With `rainout` the condensates are removed from the composition after
each equilibration and the target is reduced by the entropy they carry away, per mole of gas,
$$
s_{\mathrm{target}} = \frac{x_{\mathrm{dry}}}{x_{\mathrm{dry},0}}\,s_0 - \frac{\sum_{i \ge N_{\mathrm g}} s_i c_i}{c_{\mathrm g}} + \frac{\mathrm ds}{\mathrm d\ln p}\,\Delta\ln p ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-rainout}
where the first factor rescales the starting entropy to the moles of (conserved) dry gas and the condensate
entropies $s_i$ are those of @sec-ch03-entropy; @eq-ch03-adiabat-rainout is computed in the same
`extrapolate_dlnp` (`[C5]`).

**Stepping in height.** `extrapolate_dz` ({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dz >}})
takes the same Newton step with two additions: the pressure at the new height is not known in advance, so it starts
from the isothermal guess $p_0\exp(-g\bar M\Delta z/\mathcal R T)$ and in each pass re-evaluates hydrostatic balance
with the mean of the start and current densities,
$$
p \leftarrow p_0 - \tfrac12(\rho + \rho_0)\,g\,\Delta z, \qquad
T \leftarrow T\Bigl(1 + \frac{s_{\mathrm{target}} - s + x_{\mathrm g}\mathcal R\,\Delta\ln p}{c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}}\Bigr),
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-dz}
where $\Delta\ln p$ is the change of $\ln p$ within the pass and the term $x_{\mathrm g}\mathcal R\,\Delta\ln p$ is the
entropy change of the gas moles that the pressure update itself causes. @eq-ch03-adiabat-dz is computed in
`ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dz`. The hydrostatic update is the trapezoidal rule in $z$ with one Picard iteration per
Newton pass.

What is exact: the entropy conservation at convergence, to the stopping tolerance. What is truncated: the step is
first-order accurate in $\Delta\ln p$ or $\Delta z$ (the entropy is conserved at the end point, but the composition
that enters the latent heat is equilibrated at the end point only); the effective heat capacity is exact for the
linearised saturation conditions. The executable check is `adiabat_check.py` (`[C1]` to `[C5]`).

### Numerical method

Each step is an outer loop of at most `max-iter` passes over all cells at once. One pass is: restore $x$ to the
start of the step; `forward` at $(T, p)$, which returns $\mathsf G$; optionally drop the condensates and
renormalise; `TPX->V`, `effective_cp`, `TPV->S`; the convergence test on $\max_{\mathrm{cells}}|s_{\mathrm{target}} - s|$;
the temperature update. The `dz` variant inserts the pressure update before the temperature update.
@fig-ch03-adiabat-effective-cp shows the frozen and effective heat capacities of a water-saturated parcel of air and
the resulting dry and moist lapse rates $\mathrm d\ln T/\mathrm d\ln p = x_{\mathrm g}\mathcal R/c_p$. For the Jupiter
test card and $\Delta\ln p = -0.1$ at $200\,\mathrm K$, `DeviceTest.extrapolate_ad` runs with `max-iter` 15 and
`ftol` $10^{-8}$; the deep-Jupiter example instead calls `forward` inside its own bisection on specific entropy
(`run_column`, {{< code examples/example_jupiter_adiabat.py run_column >}}), because it needs entropy per unit mass
rather than per mole when the $\mathrm{MgSiO_3}$ reaction changes the number of molecules.

```{python}

(b) The dry (dotted black) and saturated (green) adiabatic lapse rates, the logarithmic derivative of temperature with respect to pressure, that the pressure step integrates."

: Code map of the adiabatic extrapolation. {#tbl-ch03-adiabat-code}

Walk-through of one `extrapolate_dlnp` call:

1. `TPX->V`, `TPV->S` give $s_0$; `x_dry0` is recorded for the rain-out rescaling.
2. $p \leftarrow p\,e^{\Delta\ln p}$; the start composition is saved.
3. Each pass: restore $x$; `forward` (@sec-ch04) returns $\mathsf G$; with `rainout`, the condensate
   entropies are taken from `eval_entropy_R` and the condensates zeroed; `effective_cp`; `TPV->S`; test; update.
4. After `max-iter` passes without convergence the function warns `extrapolate_dlnp does not converge` and returns
   the last state in place.

In Python, a column of forty layers by height steps (the Earth example) and a single pressure step with rain-out:

```python
# one height step, in place
thermo.extrapolate_dz(temp[:, i], pres[:, i], xfrac[:, i, :], dz=100., grav=9.8)
# one pressure step as a pseudo-adiabat
thermo.extrapolate_dlnp(temp, pres, xfrac, dlnp=-0.1, rainout=True)
# effective heat capacity, J mol^-1 K^-1, from the gain of a fresh adjustment
gain = thermo.forward(temp, pres, xfrac)
cp_eff = thermo.effective_cp(temp, pres, xfrac, gain)
```

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Each step is first order in the step size and the Newton search is capped by the card's `max-iter` (default 10),
  which the Jupiter test raises to 15 and the deep-Jupiter card to 200; a step that does not converge is returned
  with a warning only. Not measured: the error against step size.
- `effective_cp` on CUDA uses a pseudo-inverse with an absolute tolerance of $10^{-6}$ after row scaling; a gain
  matrix whose scaled singular values fall below that loses its latent term silently. Not measured.
- The entropy target is per mole of parcel (all species) in `extrapolate_dlnp`, which is not conserved along a
  reversible adiabat when a reaction changes the number of molecules (the deep-Jupiter case); the example therefore
  bypasses this routine and bisects on entropy per unit mass.
- A card that is not Kirchhoff-consistent (@sec-ch03-reference-state) gives an adiabat whose latent heating does
  not match its saturation curve; `tests/jupiter.yaml` is such a card.
- `rainout` removes all condensates every step (no partial fallout) and is untested at the pin.
:::
